title: Physics on arXiv — 7 October 2026
global_caveat: This is an inferred notable-paper ordering, not an official arXiv trending chart. Same-week citation evidence is limited; ranking uses concrete results, evidence type, cross-field relevance, publication or data status, and recency as a tie-breaker, not popularity.

sections.title: First observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay ψ(3686) → μ⁺μ⁻η′
sections.abstract: BESIII reports the first observation of this rare decay, measuring its branching fraction and comparing the muon and electron channels with vector-meson-dominance expectations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors measure B(ψ(3686) → μ⁺μ⁻η′) = (4.1 ± 1.0(stat) ± 0.4(syst)) × 10⁻⁷ and find the muon/electron channel ratio 0.22 ± 0.07, consistent with the model within 1σ.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; BESIII data collected at the BEPCII e⁺e⁻ collider
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report no significant lepton-flavor-universality violation; the branching-fraction statistical uncertainty exceeds the systematic term.

sections.title: First Measurement of Compton Scattering on ³He at HIγS
sections.abstract: The collaboration presents the first elastic Compton-scattering measurements on a ³He target, using polarized photons at two energies to probe neutron electromagnetic polarizabilities.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find chiral effective field theory agrees with the 97.1 MeV data but overpredicts the data at 61.5 MeV, motivating further theory work.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; circularly polarized quasi-monoenergetic beams from the High Intensity γ-ray Source at TUNL
sections.unique_caveat: The low-energy disagreement is unresolved; the paper reports point-to-point and normalization systematics, so the discrepancy should not be treated as a settled failure of the theory.

sections.title: Calibration-Free Broadband Reconstructive Spectrometer based on Conical Phase Modulation
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate an axicon-based reconstructive spectrometer that builds its spectral-encoding matrix computationally, removing the need for optical calibration with known-wavelength sources.
sections.claimed_result: The reported reconstruction spans 1050–1700 nm at 2.9 nm resolution, using a deterministic transmission matrix derived from conical phase modulation.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; axicon-based optical setup with broadband reconstruction measurements
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the underlying data are not publicly available at submission and may be requested from them; independent reproduction and evaluation beyond the reported setup remain open.

sections.title: The pseudospectrum for gravitational perturbations in Kerr spacetimes
sections.abstract: The authors formulate spin-2 Kerr quasinormal-mode perturbations as a non-self-adjoint eigenvalue problem and analyze how the associated pseudospectrum changes under energy norms.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find substantial Kerr spectral sensitivity persists through the norms they study and is stronger for spin-2 gravitational perturbations than for the scalar case.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical/computational; hyperboloidal formulation with two-dimensional Chebyshev collocation and a symmetrized H² energy norm
sections.unique_caveat: This is an operator-analysis result, not an observation of unstable black-hole ringdown; the proposed H^|s| norm pattern is verified here for s = 0 and s = 2, not established for every spin.

sections.title: All-Orders Classical Soft Graviton Theorems in the Newtonian Limit and Beyond
sections.abstract: The authors derive an infinite series of leading-logarithmic gravitational-wave tail terms in the Newtonian limit and examine how an existing all-orders conjecture behaves for multi-particle scattering.
sections.claimed_result: Their Newtonian-limit results agree with the prior conjecture for two-particle scattering but not in general for three or more; a beyond-Newtonian extension is proposed and passes consistency checks.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; analytic soft-theorem and scattering-amplitude analysis
sections.unique_caveat: The beyond-Newtonian all-orders statement is explicitly a conjecture, not a proof.

sections.title: An Assessment of the Triangulation Capabilities of a Multi-Site All-Sky Infrared Camera Array
sections.abstract: The Galileo Project team describes commissioning three multi-camera infrared sites and validates an unconstrained-trajectory triangulation pipeline against aircraft with ADS-B records.
sections.claimed_result: For aircraft triangulated from all three sites, 99% of recovered distances are within 5% of ADS-B references; the corresponding figure is 83% for a single site pair.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; commissioned long-wave infrared arrays, validated using ADS-B aircraft records collected during 24–30 May 2026
sections.unique_caveat: The validation concerns aircraft with external ADS-B truth data; the paper does not establish detection of anomalous or unexplained objects, and it is submitted to a journal rather than peer-reviewed in the record.

sections.title: Neural Correlation Learning for Quantum-Enhanced Sensing with Time-Independently Driven Rydberg Atom Arrays
sections.abstract: The authors propose a Bayesian/neural estimator that extracts spatial correlations from Rydberg-array measurement patterns to improve parameter sensitivity without engineered entangled-state preparation.
sections.claimed_result: In numerical demonstrations, the learned estimator saturates the classical Fisher-information Cramér–Rao bound and surpasses the standard quantum limit.
sections.evidence_type: computational; numerical Rydberg-array dynamics and estimator tests, not a hardware experiment
sections.unique_caveat: The result depends on simulated dynamics and calibration data; the paper does not demonstrate a deployed sensor or an experimental Heisenberg-limited measurement.

sections.title: Lunar radio emission from dark photon dark matter
sections.abstract: The paper proposes searching for radio emission produced when dark-photon dark matter converts at the Moon’s dielectric surface and projects sensitivity for existing and future radio telescopes.
sections.claimed_result: The author’s sensitivity projections indicate those observatories could probe parameter space not previously accessible to this strategy.
sections.evidence_type: forecast/proposal; calculated sensitivity projections for current and future radio observatories
sections.unique_caveat: This is a search strategy, not a detection or constraint from new observations; the abstract does not quantify foreground or lunar-surface systematics.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: Rare electromagnetic channels; instruments and reconstruction pipelines; gravitational-wave theory at strong-field and scattering scales; new sensor and radio search proposals.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Resolve the low-energy ³He Compton/χEFT mismatch; prove or falsify the beyond-Newtonian soft-graviton conjecture; test Kerr pseudospectral waveform implications; validate the Rydberg estimator in hardware; model backgrounds for lunar radio searches.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: The batch’s clearest near-term signals are experimental; theory papers sharpen gravitational-wave interpretation, while the quantum-sensing and lunar-dark-matter results remain simulations or projections.
